summary: mymatasan's Recording tab gains a per-camera 'Purge now' action that deletes ALL recorded footage and AI-event snapshots for that camera immediately, ignoring the configured retention period — for when an operator needs a camera's history gone right away rather than waiting on the retention sweep. It is backed by a new POST /api/recording/purge-camera endpoint (recordingService.PurgeAllForCamera for footage, deleting rows and securely removing files oldest-first, plus visionService.PurgeAlertsForCamera for the camera's alert rows and deduped snapshot files, injected as a new dependency into the recording API), and gated behind a 5-second cancellable countdown confirmation mirroring the factory-reset wipe; only the Recording tab's own segment list refreshes afterward, not the whole page. myseliasan's embedded node camera Recording tab (the mymatasan Recordings component reused over the control tunnel) gets the identical action, tunneled to the node's endpoint over the existing node proxy.
compatibility: No database schema changes. Purely additive: existing recording/retention behavior, config, and the existing 'Purge expired' (retention-based) action are unchanged. The new endpoint requires the same admin/manage authorization as other recording-management actions. Footage removal is authoritative (its error fails the request) while snapshot removal is best-effort, so a snapshot-removal hiccup can never leave footage half-purged. myseliasan's embedded Recording tab requires the adopted node to be running a build that serves POST /api/recording/purge-camera; an older node's proxy call simply fails with the existing generic error toast rather than breaking the panel.
